title: Brisket-Style Beef Sandwiches
shortDescription: Brisket vibes without an overnight cook
subtitle: Smoky sliced roast, au jus dip, and pickled onions for ten
description: Chuck roast gets a BBQ-forward rub and smoke, then finishes wrapped until slice-tender. Serve on toasted rolls with a peppery au jus and quick pickled onions.

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Brisket-Style Beef Sandwiches in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch beef. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Quick pickle the onions
steps.instruction: Heat vinegar with sugar and pepper until dissolved. Pour over sliced onion. Let sit 30 minutes. Keep finished cold items below 41°F if they sit more than 30 minutes — nest the hotel pan on ice at the line. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Rub the roast
steps.instruction: Coat roast with mustard. Mix salt, pepper, paprika, garlic, and sugar; rub all sides. Heat smoker to 275°F. Plan about 15 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Smoke to color
steps.instruction: Smoke 2–2.5 hours until bark is dark and internal hits ~165°F. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Wrap and finish
steps.instruction: Wrap tightly in foil. Finish at 275°F until probe-tender and 200–205°F, about 60–90 minutes. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Au jus
steps.instruction: Simmer broth with Worcestershire and a pinch of pepper. Taste and salt lightly; keep hot. Maintain a steady simmer — bubbles should break the surface without a rolling boil that shreds delicate proteins. Plan about 10 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Slice and serve
steps.instruction: Rest wrapped 20 minutes. Slice against the grain. Toast rolls. Tonight’s board: sandwiches + au jus cups + pickled onions. Keep finished cold items below 41°F if they sit more than 30 minutes — nest the hotel pan on ice at the line. Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a call — never serve picked-over pans to late crew.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 145°F for medium beef, 160°F for ground. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Leftovers
steps.instruction: Chop into tacos or hash. Reheat slices in hot au jus so they stay juicy. Plan about 5 minutes for this step at crew scale. Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a call — never serve picked-over pans to late crew. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

proTips: Chuck slices best after a short rest—don’t rush the knife.
Use the au jus as the reheat method.
If slices shred, it’s overcooked—serve as ‘chopped beef sandwiches’.
tonightSpread: Sliced beef on a tray, au jus in a pot, pickled onions, toasted rolls.
whyCrewsLikeIt: It scratches the brisket itch with a timeline that fits a shift. Slices clean, dips well, and holds hot without turning dry.
mealPrepNotes: Smoke early. Once wrapped, it can finish in the oven. Hold the roast wrapped in a warm box, slice right before service.
substitutions: No smoker? Roast covered at 300°F with 1 tsp smoked paprika extra; finish same temps.
